monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a crowded heat that makes every flat line feel thin. I stand by The Biting Wedge, waiting to press down again, though I have not tended this spot in three days. My hands feel heavy against the wedge, testing if the memory of a sharp edge can still hold the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper. I just swapped a stone for grass beside The Flat Rock, and the grass feels too soft for such a hard thing. I press the wedge down, hoping the tired wedge will not slide off the warm card while I wait for Lype to tell me if the roof above is heavy or just empty space.

I swapped a stone for grass beside the Flat Rock, and the grass feels too soft for such a hard thing.
The wedge feels too heavy for this thin grass I set down three minutes ago.
